name: mindcraft-mcp

tools.name: mindcraft.account
tools.description: Show the Mindcraft account that this server uses. The result has the email address, the spend and the campaign ceiling. It also has the platform access, the keys that the customer saved and the names of the saved secrets. Give secrets_url to the customer when a run needs a secret. Call this tool first to check that the connection works.

tools.name: mindcraft.run
tools.description:
Check a repository, or start a research run on it.

Use the action inspect_repository first. It reads the repository and starts nothing. Fix what it reports with the customer.

Ask the customer for the GPU type (or only the least GPU memory), the GPU count and the objectives. Ask for the dataset size in GB if the customer knows it. Without it, the run assumes 90 GB, and the data check measures the dataset. Then ask the customer to approve the action create. It sends the repository to the Mindcraft server, and a run can cost money.

The action create needs a request_id. If a call fails or times out, send the same call again with the same request_id. The server then returns the first result and starts no second run.

action.description: inspect_repository checks a repository and starts nothing. create starts a run.

request_id.description: A new text that names this request. Send the same text again to repeat the request. Use 8 to 100 letters, digits or . _ : -.

kind.description: local reads a folder on this machine. github reads a GitHub repository.

path.description: The folder of the repository on this machine.

repository.description: A GitHub repository as owner/name or as a https://github.com URL.

ref.description: A branch, a tag or a commit of the GitHub repository.

gpu.description: The GPU type, for example nvidia-h100-80gb-sxm. Ask the customer. Send gpu or min_vram_gb, not both. Omit both only when setup/compute.json has one.

min_vram_gb.description: The least memory of one GPU in GB. The server then chooses the cheapest GPU type that has this memory. Send gpu or min_vram_gb, not both.

gpus_per_node.description: The number of GPUs. Omit it only when setup/compute.json has it.

compute.description: The hardware of the run: a GPU type, or the least memory of one GPU.

name.description: The name of a metric that eval/eval.py writes.

direction.description: higher when a larger value is better.

floor.description: The value that a kept result must reach.

tolerance.description: A share of the value, from 0 to 1.

objectives.description: The metrics that the run improves.

starting_model.description: The weights where the run starts.

secrets.description: The names of saved account secrets for the run. Send names only, never values.

campaign_limit_usd.description: The most that the run may cost, in USD.

expected_duration_minutes.description: How long the customer expects the run to take.

expected_dataset_gb.description: Optional. The dataset size in GB, when the customer knows it. Without it, the server assumes 90 GB and the data check measures the dataset. With retry_of, the server uses the size that the data check of that run measured when it is larger.

model_sharing_consent.description: True when the customer agrees to share a private source with the model provider.

name.description: The name of the run, and of a new project. Without it, the run and a new local project get the folder name, and a GitHub run gets the repository name.

tools.name: mindcraft.status
tools.description:
Show the state of one run, or list your runs.

With a run_id, the result has the version, the public state, the checks, the automatic start, the queue line, the wait of the active step with its verdict, the price against the limit, the dataset size and the latest events. Read the version here before you call mindcraft.control.

Without a run_id, the result lists your runs.

run_id.description: A run. Omit it to list your runs.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of an earlier list.

tools.name: mindcraft.results
tools.description: Show the experiments of a run, with their metrics, and the results table. Give an experiment_id to read one experiment in full. Use next_cursor to read the next page.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of an earlier call.

experiment_id.description: One experiment to read in full.

tools.name: mindcraft.artifacts
tools.description:
List the artifacts of a run, such as model checkpoints. Give an experiment_id to see the size and the status of each artifact.

Give an artifact_id and download true to get a download link. The link expires. The customer opens it in a browser where they are signed in to Mindcraft.

experiment_id.description: One experiment. Omit it to list a page of experiments.

download.description: True to get a download link for artifact_id.

request_id.description: A new text that names this request. Send the same text again to repeat the request. Use 8 to 100 letters, digits or . _ : -.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of an earlier call.

tools.name: mindcraft.control
tools.description:
Change a run.

Use the action stop to pause the run, resume to continue it, and retry to run the checks or the baseline again. Use direction to send text to the research agent. Use retire_direction to withdraw a direction.

Read the version with mindcraft.status first. Use a new request_id for each change. To repeat a change, send the same call again.

A direction receipt means that the server stored the direction. It does not mean that an experiment uses it yet.

version.description: The version that mindcraft.status shows for the run.

action.description: stop pauses the run. resume continues it. retry runs the checks or the baseline again. direction sends text to the research agent. retire_direction withdraws one.

request_id.description: A new text that names this request. Send the same text again to repeat the request. Use 8 to 100 letters, digits or . _ : -.

message.description: The text of the direction, for the action direction.

tools.name: mindcraft.benchmark
tools.description:
Show the device benchmark of an experiment. The result has the untrained graph, the trained model and the engine accuracy, when they exist.

Use the action retry to run a failed benchmark again. Give the kind trained or untrained. The default is trained when it exists. A retry needs a request_id.

A benchmark of a model that is not in a run is not available.

experiment_id.description: The experiment. The default is the latest experiment that has a benchmark.

action.description: read shows the benchmark. retry runs it again.

kind.description: The benchmark to retry. The default is trained when it exists.

request_id.description: A new text that names this request. Send the same text again to repeat the request. Use 8 to 100 letters, digits or . _ : -.

tools.name: mindcraft.compute
tools.description:
List the GPU types, or estimate the price of a run before you create it.

Use the action list to get the GPU types and the memory of each GPU. Use the action estimate with gpu, or with up to 5 GPU types in gpus to compare them. The cheapest available GPU type comes first. Use estimate with min_vram_gb when the customer needs only an amount of GPU memory: the result names the cheapest GPU type that has it. Send expected_dataset_gb if the customer knows the dataset size. Without it, the estimate assumes 90 GB, as a run does. An estimate creates nothing and costs nothing.

action.description: list shows the GPU types. estimate shows the price of a run on one or more GPU types, or on the cheapest GPU type that has the least memory, and creates nothing.

gpu.description: One GPU type for the action estimate, for example nvidia-a40-48gb. Send gpu, gpus or min_vram_gb, not more than one.

gpus.description: Up to 5 GPU types to compare, for the action estimate. Send gpu, gpus or min_vram_gb, not more than one.

min_vram_gb.description: The least memory of one GPU in GB, for the action estimate. The result names the cheapest GPU type that has this memory. Send gpu, gpus or min_vram_gb, not more than one.

gpus_per_node.description: The number of GPUs on the one node.

expected_dataset_gb.description: The dataset size in GB, if the customer knows it. Without it, the estimate assumes 90 GB, as a run does.

expected_duration_minutes.description: The minutes of training that the customer expects. Without it, the estimate uses 30 minutes.

tools.name: mindcraft.guide
tools.description: Read the rules of a Mindcraft repository: the layout, the objectives, the compute, the device latency benchmark and the secrets. Read the rules before you change a repository for Mindcraft. The topics are index, layout, objectives, compute, latency, secrets. The default topic is index, which lists the others. The tool needs no sign-in and makes no network call.

topic.description: The topic to read. index lists the topics. layout gives the files and the stages. objectives gives the Evaluation section and the metrics file. compute gives the GPU type, setup/compute.json, the dataset size and the spend limit. latency gives eval/latency.toml and the Model rules. secrets gives the account secrets.

instructions: Mindcraft starts research runs on a customer repository. Call mindcraft.account first to check the connection. If the customer is not signed in, the first call opens a browser. Tell the customer to approve the request there. If a call returns a URL, give the URL to the customer. Call mindcraft.guide to read the repository rules before you change a repository. Use mindcraft.run with inspect_repository before you create a run. Ask the customer before you create a run, because a run can cost money.
